messages.subject: incoherence in MakeADFun()$fn()
parts:
Hi guys,

I'm fitting a multinomial GLMM with a specific link function in the context of repeated measures (always two measures by subject), and I have several subjects with exactly the same values (response and covariates, let's say). Thus, I was thinking instead of entering with equal subjects several times, I enter with just one and then multiply by the number of occurrences (that I'm calling here as weight).

Check this very simple data example in R:

df <- data.frame(id = c(1, 1, 2, 2),
                 rep = c(1, 2, 1, 2),
                 time = c(70, 68, 70, 68),
                 Y1 = c(1, 0, 1, 0),
                 Y2 = c(0, 1, 0, 1),
                 Y3 = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
dfW <- data.frame(id = c(1, 1),
                  rep = c(1, 2),
                  time = c(70, 68),
                  Y1 = c(1, 0),
                  Y2 = c(0, 1),
                  Y3 = c(0, 0),
                  wgt = c(2, 2))

So, instead of entering with two subjects, I enter with just one and then multiply by 2.

I'm putting the code here to make the message more readable, but I'm attaching the R and CPP files.

My CPP is as follow:

#include <TMB.hpp>
template<class Type>
Type objective_function<Type>::operator() ()
{
  using namespace density;
  // -------------------------------------------------------------------
  DATA_INTEGER(nid); // number of unique subjects
  DATA_INTEGER(nobs); // number of observations per subject (always two)
  DATA_MATRIX(Y); // nid * nobs x 3
  DATA_SPARSE_MATRIX(Z); // Matrix::bdiag() nid * nobs x nid
  DATA_VECTOR(T); // nid * nobs x 1
  DATA_SCALAR(delta);
  DATA_IVECTOR(WGT); // representativity (frequency) of each subject
  // -------------------------------------------------------------------
  PARAMETER(beta1);
  PARAMETER(beta2);
  PARAMETER(gama1);
  PARAMETER(gama2);
  PARAMETER(w1);
  PARAMETER(w2);
  PARAMETER_MATRIX(U); // nid x 4
  PARAMETER_VECTOR(sigma); // 1 x 4
  PARAMETER_VECTOR(theta); // 1 x 6
  // -------------------------------------------------------------------
  matrix<Type> RE = Z * U;
  vector<Type> eta1 = beta1 + RE.col(0).array();
  vector<Type> eta2 = beta2 + RE.col(1).array();
  vector<Type> eeta1 = exp(eta1);
  vector<Type> eeta2 = exp(eta2);
  vector<Type> p1_temp = eeta1/(1 + eeta1 + eeta2);
  vector<Type> p2_temp = eeta2/(1 + eeta1 + eeta2);
  vector<Type> middle1 = w1 * delta/(2 * T * (delta - T));
  vector<Type> middle2 = w2 * delta/(2 * T * (delta - T));
  vector<Type> x = 2 * T/delta - 1;
  vector<Type> atanh = 0.5 * log((1 + x)/(1 - x));
  vector<Type> tt1 = w1 * atanh - gama1 - RE.col(2).array();
  vector<Type> tt2 = w2 * atanh - gama2 - RE.col(3).array();
  vector<Type> ptt1 = dnorm(tt1, 0, 1, false);
  vector<Type> ptt2 = dnorm(tt2, 0, 1, false);
  vector<Type> p1 = p1_temp * middle1 * ptt1;
  vector<Type> p2 = p2_temp * middle2 * ptt2;
  vector<Type> p3 = 1 - p1 - p2;
  int size = nid * nobs;
  matrix<Type> ps(size, 3);
  ps.col(0) = p1;
  ps.col(1) = p2;
  ps.col(2) = p3;
  // -------------------------------------------------------------------
  UNSTRUCTURED_CORR_t<Type> Sigma1(theta);
  VECSCALE_t<UNSTRUCTURED_CORR_t<Type>> Sigma = VECSCALE(Sigma1, sigma);
  // -------------------------------------------------------------------
  Type nll = 0;
  vector<Type> y(Y.cols());
  vector<Type> prob(ps.cols());
  for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) {
    y = Y.row(i);
    prob = ps.row(i);
    nll -= WGT(i) * (dmultinom(y, prob, true) - Sigma(RE.row(i)));
  }
  return nll;
}

The core part is inside the loop, I compute my augmented loglik and multiply by the weight WGT.

PROBLEM: If I enter with the dataset df, without weights (WGT = 1's) I get 79.66. If I enter with dfW I get 81.65. Noise is added. I tried some different setups, I used REPORT() to see what I was getting and clearly a noise is being added.

What's happening? This should not happen, I believe. Instead of computing the same thing twice, I compute once and then multiply by 2.

library(TMB)
library(tidyverse)
library(Matrix)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
dyn.load(dynlib("laureanoModel"))
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
obj1 <- MakeADFun(data = list(nid = nrow(df)/2,
                              nobs = 2,
                              Y = as.matrix(df %>% select(Y1:Y3)),
                              Z = bdiag(replicate(nrow(df)/2,
                                                  rep(1, 2),
                                                  simplify = FALSE)),
                              T = df$time,
                              delta = max(df$time) + 0.1,
                              WGT = as.integer(c(1, 1, 1, 1))),
                  parameters = list(beta1 = -1.9,
                                    beta2 = -0.2,
                                    gama1 = 1,
                                    gama2 = 1.2,
                                    w1 = 3,
                                    w2 = 2,
                                    U = matrix(0,
                                               nrow = nrow(df)/2,
                                               ncol = 4),
                                    sigma = rep(sqrt(0.5), 4),
                                    theta = rep(0.1, 6)),
                  DLL = "laureanoModel",
                  random = "U",
                  hessian = TRUE, silent = TRUE)
obj1$fn()
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
obj2 <- MakeADFun(data = list(nid = nrow(dfW)/2,
                              nobs = 2,
                              Y = as.matrix(dfW %>% select(Y1:Y3)),
                              Z = bdiag(replicate(nrow(dfW)/2,
                                                  rep(1, 2),
                                                  simplify = FALSE)),
                              T = dfW$time,
                              delta = max(dfW$time) + 0.1,
                              WGT = as.integer(c(2, 2))),
                  parameters = list(beta1 = -1.9,
                                    beta2 = -0.2,
                                    gama1 = 1,
                                    gama2 = 1.2,
                                    w1 = 3,
                                    w2 = 2,
                                    U = matrix(0,
                                               nrow = nrow(dfW)/2,
                                               ncol = 4),
                                    sigma = rep(sqrt(0.5), 4),
                                    theta = rep(0.1, 6)),
                  DLL = "laureanoModel",
                  random = "U",
                  hessian = TRUE, silent = TRUE)
obj2$fn()

--
Tks in advance!
H

#include <TMB.hpp>
template<class Type>
Type objective_function<Type>::operator() ()
{
  using namespace density;
  // -------------------------------------------------------------------
  DATA_INTEGER(nid); // number of unique subjects
  DATA_INTEGER(nobs); // number of observations per subject (always two)
  DATA_MATRIX(Y); // nid * nobs x 3
  DATA_SPARSE_MATRIX(Z); // Matrix::bdiag() nid * nobs x nid
  DATA_VECTOR(T); // nid * nobs x 1
  DATA_SCALAR(delta);
  DATA_IVECTOR(WGT); // representativity (frequency) of each subject
  // -------------------------------------------------------------------
  PARAMETER(beta1);
  PARAMETER(beta2);
  PARAMETER(gama1);
  PARAMETER(gama2);
  PARAMETER(w1);
  PARAMETER(w2);
  PARAMETER_MATRIX(U); // nid x 4
  PARAMETER_VECTOR(sigma); // 1 x 4
  PARAMETER_VECTOR(theta); // 1 x 6
  // -------------------------------------------------------------------
  matrix<Type> RE = Z * U;
  vector<Type> eta1 = beta1 + RE.col(0).array();
  vector<Type> eta2 = beta2 + RE.col(1).array();
  vector<Type> eeta1 = exp(eta1);
  vector<Type> eeta2 = exp(eta2);
  vector<Type> p1_temp = eeta1/(1 + eeta1 + eeta2);
  vector<Type> p2_temp = eeta2/(1 + eeta1 + eeta2);
  vector<Type> middle1 = w1 * delta/(2 * T * (delta - T));
  vector<Type> middle2 = w2 * delta/(2 * T * (delta - T));
  vector<Type> x = 2 * T/delta - 1;
  vector<Type> atanh = 0.5 * log((1 + x)/(1 - x));
  vector<Type> tt1 = w1 * atanh - gama1 - RE.col(2).array();
  vector<Type> tt2 = w2 * atanh - gama2 - RE.col(3).array();
  vector<Type> ptt1 = dnorm(tt1, 0, 1, false);
  vector<Type> ptt2 = dnorm(tt2, 0, 1, false);
  vector<Type> p1 = p1_temp * middle1 * ptt1;
  vector<Type> p2 = p2_temp * middle2 * ptt2;
  vector<Type> p3 = 1 - p1 - p2;
  int size = nid * nobs;
  matrix<Type> ps(size, 3);
  ps.col(0) = p1;
  ps.col(1) = p2;
  ps.col(2) = p3;
  // -------------------------------------------------------------------
  UNSTRUCTURED_CORR_t<Type> Sigma1(theta);
  VECSCALE_t<UNSTRUCTURED_CORR_t<Type>> Sigma = VECSCALE(Sigma1, sigma);
  // -------------------------------------------------------------------
  Type nll = 0;
  vector<Type> y(Y.cols());
  vector<Type> prob(ps.cols());
  for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) {
    y = Y.row(i);
    prob = ps.row(i);
    nll -= WGT(i) * (dmultinom(y, prob, true) - Sigma(RE.row(i)));
  }
  return nll;
}

Thinking more about I think that there may be a way (given that I understand your problem correctly).
A sketch of the solution is: 
1) use the autodiff::hessian(f, u) feature of TMB to access the individuals hessians in the model.
2) Write an R function that calculates the correction of your current .cpp (which applies WGT before the Laplace approx).
3) Add this correction to your current model (R function) to obtain the post-Laplace weigthing.

Until I have implemented it, I cannot guaranty that I am correct. I think this feature (weighting with random effects)
is useful, although not often requested. Hopefully, I will have time to make an example one day.
